coverage_note: Long Latin-transliterated stretches for Medi (01:43-05:51, 30:11-30:36, 40:00-41:02, 45:38-48:16, 55:17-59:47) - read from Latin. Echo-candidates file for 2026-10-08 not present. Engine: 'talvez' 08:36 likely لابس, 'pantalon' likely بنطلون (sheet word, said in Arabic) - not tier 3; echo: شكرًا = شجر (49:10, 49:59); 52:50 'بير حجر' = غير حجر; 43:06 بهدئ = بيحرق; 32:14 زعلتكش عن = بيختلف عن. 'Adam'/الإدام 51:19 treated as the name Amsterdam per task. 06:27 'worried' is a meta English question, not tier 3. 11:35 repeat of ديرت بالي ختيفتي (Amal named على again) folded into the 09:49 row.

rows.why: He used masculine عيان for his sick fiancée; Amal recast عيانة and he took it ('Yeah, Ayana').
He made her the one hurting ('she hurts her head'); Amal recast with راسها as subject of بيوجع and he repeated it at 04:07.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say cough and Amal supplied كحة.
Answer to 'لسه عندكم شوب؟' needs عندنا; he said 'hom' (them); Amal only repeated her question and he moved on to 'shob ktir' without fixing.

rows.amal_said: Men not. ... You're worried about. You're worried from.
rows.why: 'Worried' takes من; he tried لا/الـ before نار and Amal supplied من, which he repeated ('من نار').

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.why: He offered يبدأ for a fire starting; Amal said no, there is another word, and put it aside.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say taking care; Amal supplied ديرت بالي (sheet: 'i take care of | Ana badir baali').
دير بال takes على; Amal recast بالي على خطيبتي, and at 11:45 named it again after he repeated 'ديرت بالي ختيفتي' ('بدير بالي takes على') - one row.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: He gave ديري باليك as an example; Amal recast دير بالك and labelled it the command form (sheet: 'take care / be careful | Deer baalak').
After خلينا the verb is a bare present; he used past عملنا and Amal said نعمل, which he repeated.
Non-word for 'you planned'; Amal only asked كيف يعني and he explained in English, no word supplied; sheet has 'plan | 5a66et | خطّط'.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / الدرس إنه، تفتتلي.
rows.why: 'The lesson that you planned' needs اللي, not إنه; Amal did not fix it (only asked what he meant).
Forgot sky; Amal supplied سما (sheet: 'sky | Sama').

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ ... When does the sun go up؟
rows.why: He understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; Amal said no and gave 'when does the sun go up'.

rows.medi_said: أنا نسي تلك الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.why: He said he forgot the word and tried سجر; Amal supplied فجر (sheet: 'dawn | el-fajer'); ف/س is a sound slip, so tier 0.
'I forgot' needs the I-ending نسيت; Amal let it pass (engine may have dropped the ت).
تلك is MSA, not her Levantine 'that' (هاي/هديك); she let it pass.
For 'other than' he said غير لو; Amal said 'No لو. غير.' (لو belongs in حتى لو).
غير never takes el- on the noun after it; Amal recast غير شمس و يوم twice (20:12, 20:30).
rows.english: other than the sun and the day

rows.medi_said: بس في الـ، الـ، الليل سما. / في الليل سما،
rows.why: The sky is a known thing and needs el-; Amal recast السما بالليل and he rebuilt 'الـ سما بي الليل'.
Forgot 'dark at night'; Amal supplied عتمة (sheet: 'darkness | 3etme').
'One' follows the noun (شمس واحدة); Amal only echoed واحدة and said great job, so let pass.
After a feminine noun تاني must be تانية; Amal echoed تاني as a prompt and he fixed to تانية, she said mm.
Fronted نجمة needs the pointer -ha on the verb; Amal prompted and he said بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer').

rows.medi_said: since is لـ-لـ-lessa, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He asked for 'since', guessing لسه then لا; Amal said no and supplied من.
Past 'it rained' (feminine) is مطرت; Amal recast and he repeated 'Matarat'.

rows.medi_said: آآ، بيد من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: 'Different' takes عن, not من; Amal said عن twice and he used 'بيد and (عن) الهاوا هناك'. engine wrote زعلتكش for her line.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.why: آخر + el- = 'the end of'; 'the last time' is آخر مرة with no el-, as Amal explained.
مرة is feminine so كان must be كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he fixed to كانت.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين ... would be for the last three years. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي for 'ago'; Amal said no, that means 'the last three years', 'ago' is قبل.
The past of 'it snowed' is تلّجت; Amal recast with the doubled ل; could be only sound shape (F3).

rows.medi_said: Il hawa aju ktir il sabah
rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟
rows.why: هوا is masculine singular but he used plural اجو; after Amal's 'إيش يعني؟' he fixed to 'Aja' ('it's singular'), and she then steered to 'كان قوي'.
rows.english: The wind came a lot this morning.

rows.amal_said: بهدئ. Do you know that بهدئ also means it burns?
rows.why: Asked for spicy, he got only 'به-' and Amal supplied the word (engine wrote بهدئ for بيحرق).

rows.medi_said: El nar, nar heret me. Does that count correct?
rows.why: The object 'me' rides on the verb (حرقتني); he left English 'me' and asked, Amal recast النار حرقتني.
'I cleaned it' needs the object ending -ha; Amal prompted 'It.', he said 'Nadabet ha' and she confirmed نظفتها.
Didn't-know: he asked for the plants word; Amal supplied زريعة (sheet: 'plants (domestic) | Zri3a').
Forgot stones; Amal supplied حجر (sheet: 'stone | 7ajar').

rows.amal_said: صخر is under the sea, under the ocean.
rows.why: He did not know rocks; Amal supplied صخر (sheet: 'rock | Sa5ra').
He meant the streets (plural) but said singular الشارع with feminine قديمة; Amal recast الشوارع and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: He added a verb 'made' for 'are (made of) stone'; Amal said just حجر ('Are stone'): no verb needed, her line الشوارع ... في أمريكا حجر.
rows.english: The streets in America are stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني; حجر تاني means 'another stone'; Amal recast after he switched from his right first form.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: 'My favorite' standing alone is المفضل عندي (el- + عندي), not مفضل لي; Amal recast and repeated 'الـ، المفضل عندي'.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: Adjective goes after the noun; Amal recast الحجر المفضل and named it an adjective.
A noun with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal: 'No ال first'.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: For 'this lesson is my favorite' the adjective takes el- and follows الدرس; Amal explained and recast هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: For 'isn't here' he used في (there is); Amal said مش هون and explained في means 'there is'.
Garbled form of the thank-you phrase; Amal answered with the standard يعطيك العافية, which may just be her reply, not a fix.
